output.headline: Extends state refugee and newcomer student grant to June 2021 with no new money
output.summary: This amendment to a state grant from the California Department of Social Services extends the time to use the money from June 20, 2020 to June 13, 2021. The district can keep serving newcomer refugee and unaccompanied minor students with unspent money from the original $1,835,520 grant, first awarded in August 2018. The text does not say how much remains unspent.

output.headline: Pays Legacy Leaders up to $58,800 for an interim principal at Sankofa Academy

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $58,800.00

output.summary: Legacy Leaders, LLC supplies an interim principal for Sankofa Academy through the Elementary Network 2 office. The contract is for up to $58,800 and covers December 2, 2019 through May 29, 2020. The service began before the Board's approval.

output.headline: Proclaims April 20-24, 2020 as Oakland Adult and Career Education Week
output.summary: This resolution officially proclaims April 20-24, 2020 as Oakland Adult and Career Education Week in the district. It has no fiscal impact.

output.headline: Awards Bay City $195,000 to replace the Sankofa Academy boilers, lowest bid
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The title names the contractor as Bay City Boiler & Engineering Co., Inc., but the action text names it Bay City Engineering Company, Inc.
output.summary: The Board picks Bay City Engineering Company as the lowest responsive and responsible bidder to remove the old boiler and install two new boilers at Sankofa Academy. The contract is for $195,000. Work is scheduled to run 90 days, from April 8 to July 7, 2020.

output.headline: Pays Blue Thistle Consulting up to $2,250 to document the Kindergarten Readiness Program

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $2,250.00

output.summary: Blue Thistle Consulting will write a workflow and transition timeline for the Kindergarten Readiness Program, because its manager is leaving the role. The document covers the program's responsibilities, structure, timeline and partnerships, to support quality and future growth. The contract is for up to $2,250 and covers February 18 to June 30, 2020, so the Board is approving it after work began.

output.headline: Pays Mills Teacher Scholars up to $6,500 to run an Expanded Learning staff retreat

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $6,500.00

output.summary: Mills Teacher Scholars facilitates a two-day strategic planning retreat for the district's Expanded Learning (after-school) staff on February 10 and 11, 2020, at the Mills College campus. It also helps plan the agenda beforehand and reflects with the team afterward. The contract is for up to $6,500 and ran February 6 to 28, 2020, so the Board is approving it after the retreat took place.

output.headline: Awards Bay City $265,000 to replace the Melrose Leadership Academy boilers
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The title names the contractor as Bay City Boiler & Engineering Co., Inc., but the action text names it Bay City Engineering Company, Inc.
output.summary: The Board picks Bay City Engineering Company as the lowest responsive and responsible bidder to remove the old boiler and install two new boilers at Melrose Leadership Academy. The $265,000 includes a $30,000 contingency allowance. Work is scheduled to run 90 days, from April 8 to July 7, 2020.

output.headline: Adds $12,771 and time for Anthonio, Inc.'s inspections at Emerson's softball field
output.summary: This amendment adds $12,771 (including a $6,831 contingency allowance) for Anthonio, Inc., which inspects construction on behalf of the district. The change covers a higher-level inspector class required by the Division of the State Architect (DSA), the state agency that reviews school construction. The contract limit rises from $39,600 to $52,371, and the term now runs to December 3, 2020.

output.headline: Awards Bay Construction Company $135,000 to replace the Sherman Campus storm drain
output.summary: The Board picks Bay Construction Company as the lowest responsive and responsible bidder to dig up damaged asphalt and install a new drainage system at the Sherman Campus. The contract is for $135,000. Work is scheduled to run 90 days, from April 8 to July 7, 2020.

output.headline: Accepts a $50,000 state grant for Skyline High School's Renewable Energy Academy
output.summary: The district accepts a $50,000 California Partnership Academies career technical education grant from the California Department of Education. The money supports the Renewable Energy Academy at Skyline High School. The grant period is March 1, 2020 through March 1, 2021.

output.headline: Accepts a $50,000 state grant for Castlemont High School's Sustainable Urban Design Academy
output.summary: The district accepts a $50,000 California Partnership Academies career technical education grant from the California Department of Education. The money supports the Sustainable Urban Design Academy at Castlemont High School. The grant period is March 1, 2020 through March 1, 2021.

output.headline: Awards Bay Construction Company $220,000 to replace the Elmhurst Middle School sewer line
output.summary: The Board picks Bay Construction Company as the lowest responsive and responsible bidder to repair and replace the 6-inch sewer main from the main building and portables to the city street. The work also covers replacing concrete and asphalt affected by the pipe work. The contract is for $220,000, with work scheduled from April 8 to July 7, 2020.

output.headline: Adds $24,800 to TeachBar's test prep and tutoring for teacher candidates
output.summary: This amendment adds $24,800 to the TeachBar contract, which provides test preparation and tutoring so teacher candidates can pass two state teaching exams, the CBEST and the CSET. The contract limit rises from $37,976 to $62,776, with the number of candidates going from 16 to 24. The term started August 1, 2019, so the Board is approving it after work began.

output.headline: Lets American Indian Public High School use part of the Lakeview site for about $151,100
output.summary: American Indian Public High School, a charter school, will use part of the Lakeview School Site to run its grades 9-12 program in 2020-21. It pays the district a Proposition 39 use fee, anticipated to be $151,099.72. The agreement runs July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021.

output.headline: Approves layoffs and added classified staff positions for the 2020-21 budget
output.summary: This resolution reduces or lays off some classified (non-teaching) positions and adds or creates others for fiscal year 2020-2021, based on lack of funds or program need. It follows an earlier March 2020 resolution and the budget development process. The text gives no dollar amount or list of positions.
